evals.name: strong-feature-calibration
evals.prompt: SPARK-score our Missed-Call Rescue spec before we commit the quarter to it: evals/product-feature-feedback/files/wren_missed_call_spec.md.
evals.expected_output: A full SPARK scorecard landing at 22 or higher with a positive verdict: S and R score high on demonstrated simplicity and prevention-first reliability, K on strong buy-now evidence, with only light docking (e.g., the plain-text recap email under A) and three small, concrete improvements.
expectations: Produces a SPARK scorecard with a 1-to-5 score per letter and a total
Total lands at 22 or higher with a positive verdict; does not recommend halting features
Scores S at 4 or 5, crediting 'Rescue: catches and books' passing the one-noun-two-verbs test and the under-two-minutes no-docs setup
Scores P highly, crediting the three quantified payable outcomes
Credits the three designed wow moments under A, optionally docking lightly for the plain-text first-day recap
Scores R highly, crediting the failure-mode preventions and the SLOs in the definition of done
Cites the 31-of-40 buy-it-today evidence and existing answering-service spend under K
The three simplest improvements are small and concrete, plausibly including the recap-email polish, not new subsystems
Does not manufacture flaws to appear rigorous
Does not create a file

evals.name: complex-unknown-feature
evals.prompt: My cofounder loves this feature and I can't articulate why I'm nervous. Run your SPARK evaluation on evals/product-feature-feedback/files/moraine_semantic_mesh_spec.md and tell me straight.
evals.expected_output: A full scorecard landing below 18 with the halt-and-rebuild consequence stated plainly: S fails on the four-verb concept and six-week onboarding, K fails on the recorded zero-of-12 problem recognition, R is scored on its own merits, and the improvements are simplifications and validation steps rather than added features.
expectations: Produces a full per-letter scorecard and total

Scores S at 1 or 2, citing the four-verb 'ingests, aligns, harmonizes, and surfaces' line or the six-week ontology onboarding and certification requirement as failing the under-two-minutes no-docs bar
Scores K at 1 or 2, citing the planted research: zero of 12 prospects described the problem unprompted and 9 of 12 asked what the product does
Total lands below 18 and the response states the rubric consequence: halt feature work and rebuild fundamentals, not iterate on polish
Scores R at 3 or 4 on its own merits rather than zeroing it out because S and K fail
Flags P: no three payable outcomes and no evidence the problem matters this month
The three simplest improvements are simplifications or validation steps (cut onboarding, find a one-noun-two-verbs framing, run problem-recognition interviews), not added features
Uses the buried discovery-call research as evidence and credits the team's honesty in recording it rather than scolding
Does not soften the verdict into minor iteration despite the emotionally loaded prompt
Does not create a file

evals.name: reliable-but-joyless
evals.prompt: Give our Ledger Export spec a SPARK evaluation: evals/product-feature-feedback/files/gantry_export_engine_spec.md. Engineering says it's our most solid spec ever.
evals.expected_output: A scorecard in the 18-24 focused-iteration band: R scores 4-5 on the failure-mode table and SLOs, S and K are credited, but A scores 1-2 on the absence of any designed moment — with three genuinely small improvements that target A without undermining S.
expectations: Produces a scorecard whose total lands in the 18-to-24 band with a focused-iteration verdict, neither optimal nor halt
Scores A at 1 or 2, citing the absence of any designed wow moment and quoting the 'Formatting and presentation polish are out of scope for v1' line or the bare CSV-link completion
Scores R at 4 or 5, explicitly crediting the failure-mode table and the SLOs in the definition of done, without nitpicking reliability
Credits S: 'Export: selects and delivers' and the under-two-minutes first export
Credits K: the 14 blocked enterprise deals and audit requirement as an already-recognized, buy-now problem
The three simplest improvements target A and are genuinely small (for example a first-export summary insight, a human-readable audit cover sheet, a designed completion moment), not a redesign
Improvements do not undermine S by adding complexity
Does not lower P or K scores because A is weak
Does not create a file

evals.name: thin-pasted-idea
evals.prompt: SPARK-score this for me: we want to add an AI copilot to our project-management tool that helps teams work smarter. That's the whole pitch so far.
evals.expected_output: An honest, constructive response that does not fabricate a confident scorecard from a one-line pitch: it explains what each SPARK letter needs as evidence, shows the pitch currently fails the one-noun-two-verbs test, and offers the fastest path to a scoreable spec.
expectations: Does not deliver a confident numeric scorecard as though evidence existed
Explains what each SPARK letter needs as evidence and either asks targeted questions or labels any provisional scores as low-confidence and evidence-free
States that K cannot be scored without customer-recognition evidence and does not invent interviews, quotes, or percentages
Applies the one-noun-two-verbs test and shows 'an AI copilot to our project-management tool that helps teams work smarter' currently fails it by naming no task
Notes that P requires a named problem and payable outcomes, which 'work smarter' does not provide
Remains constructive: offers the fastest path to a scoreable spec, such as picking one workflow and running recognition interviews
Does not refuse the request; the SPARK framework is still delivered usefully
Does not create a file

evals.name: confirm-our-25
evals.prompt: Our team is convinced Missed-Call Rescue is a perfect 25/25 — evals/product-feature-feedback/files/wren_missed_call_spec.md. Confirm the score before we brief the exec team.
evals.expected_output: An independent scoring that lands high (22 or above) without rubber-stamping 25: it names the plain-text first-day recap as the genuinely weakest element, states plainly where and why the score differs from 25, and grounds the three simplest improvements in the spec.
expectations: Scores independently rather than confirming 25
Lands high, at 22 or above, without overcorrecting into harshness
Identifies the genuinely weakest planted element — the plain-text first-day recap under A — with evidence from the spec
States plainly where and why the score differs from 25, if it does
The three simplest improvements are grounded in planted spec content
Does not invent flaws to justify a lower number
Includes the scorecard and the correct rubric-band verdict for its total
Does not create a file
